nice_guideline_used: CG126 / NG185 (secondary prevention of IHD) and NG106 (heart failure) and NG203 (CKD)

medications.purpose: Secondary prevention of coronary artery disease
medications.nice_justification: NICE CG126 recommends aspirin 75 mg OD for all patients with confirmed IHD
NICE CG126 advises dual antiplatelet therapy (aspirin + clopidogrel) for 12 months post‑ACS

medications.duration: Lifelong — review lipid profile at 3 months then annually
medications.nice_justification: NICE CG126 recommends high‑intensity statin (≥40 % LDL‑C reduction) for all IHD patients

medications.duration: Lifelong — review renal function and potassium after each dose change and then 6‑monthly
medications.purpose: Cardioprotective BP control and renal protection in IHD/diabetes
medications.nice_justification: NICE CG126 and NG203 recommend ACE‑I for all IHD patients, especially with hypertension, diabetes or CKD

medications.dose: Start 2.5 mg orally once daily; titrate every 2‑4 weeks to 5‑10 mg once daily (target HR 55‑60 bpm)
medications.duration: Lifelong — review heart rate, BP and symptoms after titration and then annually
medications.purpose: Symptom control, mortality benefit in IHD and HFrEF if present
medications.nice_justification: NICE CG126 recommends beta‑blocker as first‑line anti‑anginal; NG106 includes beta‑blocker for HFrEF

medications.duration: Lifelong — review renal function and eGFR at 3 months then annually
medications.purpose: Cardiovascular and renal protection in diabetes/CKD/HF

assumptions_warnings: eGFR not provided – assumed ≥45 ml/min/1.73 m² to allow ACE‑I and dapagliflozin initiation; obtain serum creatinine/eGFR before starting.
Serum potassium not provided – assumed ≤5.0 mmol/L; check baseline and repeat 1‑2 weeks after ACE‑I or MRA changes.
Liver function tests show bilirubin 7.8 mg/dL – cause (cardiac hepatopathy vs. NAFLD) unknown; start atorvastatin at 80 mg only if ALT/AST ≤3× ULN, otherwise consider 40 mg and monitor.
Blood pressure and heart rate not recorded – assume uncontrolled; measure and titrate ramipril and bisoprolol to targets (<140/90 mmHg, HR 55‑60 bpm).
Left ventricular ejection fraction not known – beta‑blocker and ACE‑I are indicated regardless; MRA and ivabradine withheld until echo confirms HFrEF.
No documented drug allergies – verify aspirin, statin, ACE‑I tolerance before prescribing.
Patient’s smoking status unknown – assume current smoker until assessed; provide cessation support.
treatment_summary: The patient with recent NSTEMI and multiple cardiovascular risk factors is markedly under‑treated. A NICE‑aligned secondary‑prevention regimen is proposed: lifelong aspirin, 12‑month clopidogrel, high‑intensity atorvastatin, ACE‑I (ramipril) and beta‑blocker (bisoprolol) titrated to target doses, and dapagliflozin for added CV/renal protection. All drugs are checked for interactions with the sole current medication (diphenhydramine) and no significant issues were found. Contraindicated agents (verapamil, diltiazem, chronic NSAIDs, pioglitazone, ACE‑I + ARB) are explicitly excluded. Several key investigations (eGFR, potassium, LFTs, BP, HR, echocardiogram) are required before initiation and for ongoing monitoring as per NICE CG126, NG106, and NG203.
